key_insight: The paper proposes swapping entanglement from local qubit–magnon pairs into a remote bipartite magnonic cat state, enabling nonlocal bosonic quantum states across separated hybrid devices.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to long-distance quantum links in hybrid magnon–qubit hardware, relevant for scalable quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.
method: Prepare two spatially separated transmon–YIG hybrid subsystems with local magnon-qubit entanglement.
Perform a Bell-state measurement on the qubits to swap entanglement onto the remote magnon modes.
Characterize the resulting state via Wigner-function tomography using joint displaced parity measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a concrete protocol and a state-reconstruction method, using tomography/Wigner-function evaluation as the main characterization tool rather than experimental performance data.
watch_item: The scheme relies on high-fidelity Bell-state measurements, coherent magnon control, and parity-based tomography, which may be challenging to implement with low noise and loss in practice.
paper_title: Nonlocal Magnonic Cat States in Hybrid Magnon-Qubit Architectures
